newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Algarve tourism had bad 1996, but future brighter.
newsitem.headline: Algarve tourism had bad 1996, but future brighter.

text.p: Sun-and-sand tourism in the Algarve region of Portugal had a poor 1996 because of economic pressures on foreign visitors, but looks set for a mild recovery next year, a local tourism group said on Thursday.
"1996 was a bad year for tourism, although it wasn't as bad as had been forecast at the start of the season," a study by the Association of Hotels and Tourism Businesses of the Algarve (AHETA) said.
A stronger escudo hit many tourists in the pocket, AHETA said. Uncertainties about job security also dampened demand.

The decline was largely due to a drop in British visitors, who account for almost a third of all tourists to the Algarve. However, prospects for British arrivals in 1997 have been brightened by a strengthening of sterling against the escudo.

Tourism in the Algarve region of southern Portugal brings in some eight million visitors and generates 600 billion escudos ($3.9 billion) in revenue a year, about 60 percent of Portugal's total tourism receipts.
The region has long stretches of sandy beaches, many golf courses, marinas and a well-developed tourist infrastructure ranging from five-star hotels to basic self-catering apartments.

The number of visitors passing through the region's main airport at Faro fell 2.2 percent in 1996, compared with 1995, to 3.53 million people, AHETA said. It forecast a 3.5 percent increase in the number of passengers in 1997.
